You want them to hear?" balloon does sit flat against the top border: pixel samples at x 1150/1250/1350 show the frame line at y 869-872 and the balloon's white starting at y 873, so the balloon's outline merges into the frame. The text is fully readable, with about 40 px of white above the cap height, the tail points cleanly at Nagoji's mouth, and the balloon covers none of his face. At print size this is a small tangent, polish at most, not a major problem. Refuted as a major issue. If anything, it is a minor note to lower the balloon a few pixels.

refuted.description: The POV shot does not look straight up the ladder at a guard on its top rungs. The guard stands at nearly eye level in a vertical, door-like opening, with a plank door and an iron ring handle beside him. That contradicts the overhead hatch set up in 1.4, 1.5, 2.2 and 7.1, and loses the 'coming down the ladder' staging that 7.1 depends on.
refuted.reason: The claim does not hold up on page 6, panel 5. I zoomed to 2x and found every beat from script 6.5 in the art. It is a low-angle POV from below. The undersides of several ladder treads, with light between them, run across the bottom of the frame. The guard's boot rests on one of those rungs and his left hand grips the ladder rail, so he is on the top rungs coming down, not standing level at a door. His figure is a lightning-backlit silhouette, the brim and crest of his morion read clearly, and the musket muzzle swings straight at the camera. The angle is steep rather than truly vertical, which is a fair way to draw "looking straight up the ladder". The hatch is not inconsistent with the rest of the chapter either. Page 2, panel 1 already draws the companion as a steep ladder rising to an opening, with a large iron ring on the post beside it. Page 2, panel 4 shows the stair climbing to an upright-looking opening full of sky. The ring-handled plank panel on the right of 6.5 reads as the opened hatch cover or companion door, which matches that earlier staging. Page 7, panel 1 then shows the same guard on the ladder below the opening, so the handoff from 6.5 to 7.1 works. At print size a reader sees an armed guard above Nagoji on the ladder, aiming down. Neither the story nor the continuity breaks.

minors.description: Keshavrao reads older than the locked 'about nineteen, rounder, softer face'. In this close-up his face is broader and more weathered than in his other panels and on sheet 07-keshavrao-v15c, so the boy beat ('the ghost of a smile') plays more like a man in his late twenties.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-04.png around (930-1690, 360-1160): Keshavrao has crow's-feet and lines under the eyes, a creased brow and a wide jaw and neck. In 3.5, 8.2 and 9.1 his face is younger and narrower.

minors.description: Keshavrao is drawn as tall and as broad and muscular as Nagoji. The size contrast the lock requires ('clearly younger, smaller and thinner than Nagoji; narrow shoulders') is lost in the one panel where both stand full-figure side by side.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-05.png at (250-1720, 2030-2540): Keshavrao (right) stands with his hands on his hips and has heavy deltoids and arms. His head sits at the same height as Nagoji's (left) and his shoulder width matches. Hair, tunic and moustache still identify him.

minors.description: The bearded background prisoner between Nagoji and Keshavrao wears a gold drop ear stud, and he has long curly black hair. Both are Nagoji's identifying marks, so this prisoner reads as a bearded Nagoji double right next to the real one.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-04.png at (800-1080, 2340-2540): the 'We will drown down here.' speaker has a small gold drop earring on his visible ear and curly hair, sitting directly beside Nagoji, who wears the same gold stud.

minors.description: Nagoji's ear stud is off-model. In 7.4 it is drawn as a tiny silver/white pin, not the small gold stud from the sheet. In 7.1 his visible ear has no stud at all.
minors.evidence: Zoom of page-07.png at (770-900, 1940-2060): a pale silver point on his right earlobe. Zoom at (340-460, 640-760): the ear in 7.1 is bare. The gold stud is correct in 7.2 and on pages 1-6 and 8-10.

minors.description: Keshavrao's required rain-washed graze at the hairline is missing. The script uses it to mark that he was hurt in the wave.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09.png at (800-1300, 380-700): his forehead and hairline are clean, with only rain on the skin. There is no graze anywhere.

minors.description: Nagoji's torn sleeveless ochre tunic has turned into a long-sleeved, robe-like garment. Both forearms are wrapped in ochre sleeves down to the manacles, which departs from the captivity sheet he wears everywhere else. In 9.3 his face is cut to a moustache tip in the corner, so only the costume identifies him.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-09.png at (150-1150, 1320-1720): at the left edge, both of Nagoji's arms are in loose ochre sleeves to the wrist. In 9.4 the ochre cloth drapes like a cape over his back and far arm. Compare 9.2 and 10.5, where the tunic is sleeveless.

minors.description: Nagoji's head is jammed against the top panel border. The crown and forehead are cropped, which shrinks the bared-teeth reaction the panel is built around.
minors.evidence: page-05.png at about (800-1300, 870-1000): the panel's top edge cuts through Nagoji's hairline just above the brows. His face takes up only a small corner beside the balloon.

minors.description: In both wide shots the top of Nagoji's head is cropped by the panel border, so his face is pressed against the frame edge.
minors.evidence: Crop of page-10.png at (400-800, 360-900): the 10.1 frame line cuts through the top of his head. Crop at (380-1300, 1680-2000): in 10.4 his hair and the top of his head run into the top border.

minors.description: Nagoji's costume drifts on this page. The torn ochre sleeveless tunic grows into a large ochre wrap that drapes over his back and thighs like a shawl. In 9.5 the knee pinning the coil is bare skin ringed with ochre rags, where it should be under the cream dhoti. On pages 1 to 8 the tunic stops at the hips and the cream dhoti covers his legs.
minors.evidence: 9.4: ochre cloth hangs from his shoulders over his thigh and down to the deck (about x=130 to 400, y=1330 to 1480). 9.5: the knee at about x=400,y=1700 is bare skin wrapped in tattered ochre, with no cream cloth. Compare 8.1, where the tunic ends at the hip and the cream dhoti covers his legs.

minors.description: The ladder changes design on the same page. In 6.4 it is a rope-lashed ladder with round rungs. In 6.2, and again in 7.1 and 7.2, it is a timber ladder with square rails and flat plank treads. It is the same swaying ladder throughout pages 6 and 7.
minors.evidence: 6.4: round rungs bound with rope lashings at each joint (about x=530 to 600, y=1500 to 1800). 6.2: flat-plank rungs between square rails at the left (about x=170 to 330, y=600 to 980). 7.1: a flat-tread plank ladder.

minors.description: Props and setting on this page do not match 2.1. The musket has a dark butt with an iron rim and iron barrel bands, but in 2.1 it has a large brass butt plate and brass fittings (it has brass again in 6.3). The ladder has become a broad open staircase with water running down it into open sky, where 2.1 and 2.2 show a steep ladder up to a hatch under an awning. Crates and barrels also replace the pens that stand beside the musket in 2.1.
minors.evidence: 2.1 musket: brass butt plate at about x=200 to 370, y=870 to 1060. 2.4 musket: iron-rimmed dark butt at about x=120 to 160, y=1690, with three iron bands along the barrel. 2.4 stair: a wide stair with rails and a cascade, opening to cloud (about x=1030 to 1210, y=1580 to 1810).

minors.description: The script calls for 'the broken ladder' at the empty hatch, but the ladder here is short, narrow and intact. The hatch is also drawn as a long trough-like opening, much larger than the square hatch in 8.2 and 9.1.
minors.evidence: An intact rung ladder at about x=880 to 950, y=490 to 620, inside a long rectangular opening that runs most of the panel width (about x=590 to 1210, y=470 to 620).

minors.description: The bible and script fix the collar as a hinged iron collar with the ring at the side, but most panels put the ring at the front of the throat, often with chain hanging straight down the chest. Only a few panels place it at the side, so the ring jumps between positions through the chapter.
minors.evidence: Ring at the front: 1.1 (a chain hangs from the front ring down to Nagoji's lap), 1.2, 2.1, 3.4, 4.2, 9.4, 10.3 and 10.5. Ring at the side: 8.2, 9.1 and 10.2.

minors.description: The covering on Nagoji's left forearm switches on and off within the page. In 5.3 and 5.5, and in 3.2 and 10.1, it is a full-length ochre sleeve on the left arm. In 5.4, between those two panels, the tunic is sleeveless and the forearm is bare above the bandage. No brand is drawn anywhere, which is correct. The covering just needs one consistent form, either the script's ragged flap or the sleeve.
minors.evidence: 5.5: an ochre sleeve covers the left arm from shoulder to wrist (about x=390 to 470, y=1560 to 1640). 5.4: the left forearm is bare skin between the elbow and the bandage (about x=440 to 520, y=1150 to 1240).

minors.description: The extras' costume and the hold layout break continuity. On pages 1 and 2 the prisoners wear grey, brown and off-white ragged tunics in small plank pens. In 3.1 they are bare-chested in loincloths, lined along a long flooded central aisle that reads as a galley's rowing benches.
minors.evidence: 3.1: rows of shirtless men in white loincloths either side of a central water channel. 1.1 and 2.1: tunic-clad prisoners in short pens.

minors.description: A background prisoner wears a wrapped rust-red turban, which is Nagoji's signature commander colour. Nagoji is deliberately bare-headed in captivity, and this extra is right beside him.
minors.evidence: A prisoner at about x=950 to 1010, y=760 to 790 with a rust-red cloth wrapped on his head, two places along from Nagoji.

minors.description: Keshavrao's lower garment changes on the same page. In 2.1 he wears the off-white dhoti of his approved sheet down to the ankle. In 2.3 his legs show only grey-brown knee-length rags and bare shins.
minors.evidence: 2.1: off-white dhoti to the ankles at about x=560 to 760, y=600 to 730. 2.3: grey-brown ragged cloth over his knees with bare shins at about x=990 to 1200, y=1380 to 1520.

minors.description: The rain-washed graze at Keshavrao's hairline that the script asks for (the softened version of the novel's head wound) is missing. His forehead is clean.
minors.evidence: Close-up of his face at about x=620 to 720, y=290 to 410: no graze or mark at the hairline.

minors.description: The stripped bandages read well, but the palms look like ordinary skin, not the 'reddened and burned' palms the script specifies. In 10.1 the palms are clearly red, so the injury seems to appear between panels.
minors.evidence: 9.5 palms at about x=650 to 780 and x=860 to 980, y=1620 to 1760: natural warm skin tone. 10.1 palms at about x=380 to 400 and x=510 to 530, y=430 to 470: bright red.

minors.description: The guard wears a broad leather waist belt with a large brass buckle as well as his cross-belt. The script specifies no wide belt for the ship guards, so that none of them reads as João.
minors.evidence: A waist belt with a big square buckle at about x=490 to 640, y=420 to 470, under the cross-belt.

minors.description: The background crew don't match 8.1. In 8.1 the sailors wear loose shirts, slops, head cloths and sashes. In 8.3 they wear dark waistcoats with leather belts, and one wears a cocked hat, which reads as a stock pirate crew.
minors.evidence: Figures at the upper left of 8.3 (about x=125 to 450, y=1200 to 1340): black waistcoats, belts and a dark cocked hat on the centre figure.

minors.description: A prisoner has a red smear on his forehead. It reads as blood or as a tilak mark, which conflicts with the no-blood rule.
minors.evidence: The bearded prisoner, third from the left, at about x=650 to 700, y=965 to 990: a red mark across his forehead.

minors.description: Iron hangs steeply from overhead to a neck. After the ring tears, the pen chain still runs taut from the ring in the beam almost straight down to the collar of the bald prisoner at the right end of the row, so a chain from a ring overhead ends at a man's throat. The script wants the chain end to drop and sag into the water here, with no chain near vertical above a head.
minors.evidence: page-05.png, panel 5.2, top-right. The ring is at about native (1530,400) and the chain descends at roughly 65-70 degrees to the bald man's collar at about native (1610,690). It does not sag.

minors.description: The rust-red blotches on Nagoji's hand bandages can read as dried blood stains in this tight insert.
minors.evidence: page-06.png, panel 6.3, left hand on the musket stock at about native (420-640, 1640-1880). Orange-brown spots are scattered over the white wrappings, much heavier than the grime on his bandages elsewhere in the chapter (for example 1.1 and 2.3). Shift them to grey-brown grime or remove them.

minors.description: (Outside the standing-rules lens) The caption order is ambiguous. The second caption, 'It was the change in the way the ship moved.', is at the left edge, and the first, 'The first warning was not the shout of a sailor...', is at the right. A left-first reader takes the answer before the setup.
minors.evidence: page-01.png, panel 1.1. The left box is at display y 370-435 and the right box at y 283-375. Put the first caption at top-left, or stack both on the right.

minors.description: (Outside the standing-rules lens) The 'Forgive me.' balloon is placed left of both captions, so it reads before 'On the field there was no room for hesitation.' and 'This was my field now.'. The script orders the two captions first and 'Forgive me.' as the closing line.
minors.evidence: page-10.png, panel 10.3. The balloon is at display x 275-430 and the captions at x 590-1210 along the top edge.

minors.description: The script calls for jagged, overlapping shout balloons coming from above and off panel. They are lettered as smooth round balloons side by side, and their tails stop mid-panel on the boot shadows instead of reaching the top border. The first balloon also breaks badly, leaving 'haul!' alone on its own line.
minors.evidence: 'Reef the sails! Haul, / haul!' and 'Tie that down! Move, you son of a dog!' are ordinary rounded balloons at about y 1270-1450, with tails ending around y 1170-1200, well inside the panel.

minors.description: The guard's balloons are nearly level, and the second one is the larger and further left, so the threat can be read before 'Quiet down there.' The line also wraps poorly, leaving the single word 'over.' on its last line.
minors.evidence: 'If any of you break your chains...' is at about x 150-771, y 1849-2078. 'Quiet down there. No shouting. No prayers.' is at about x 834-1390, y 1768-1890.

minors.description: The first balloon is flattened against the top border, as if clipped, and its tail tip lands on Nagoji's brow. Which balloon reads first depends only on the right one sitting about 100 px higher than the left.
minors.evidence: 'Storms break ships. When wood breaks, bolts pull out. Chains go loose.' runs flush into the top border at about x 990-1647, y 1485-1654, and its tail ends at Nagoji's eyebrow. 'The men above...' sits lower left, at about x 150-730, y 1600-1830.

minors.description: The script tags both of Nagoji's orders as '(in Marathi)', and the adaptation notes say the tag is deliberate. The lettering carries no language marker, such as angle brackets or a translation note.
minors.evidence: The balloons 'Hold to the beams! Hook your arms over the wood.' and 'Do not let the chain drag you.' are plain balloons with no marker.

minors.description: The second balloon is set in five narrow lines and fills about a third of the small panel. It covers Nagoji's crouched body and the plank behind him that the script says bows inward.
minors.evidence: The 'You have seen the dungeon. That is what awaits us...' balloon is at about x 448-851, y 744-1077, inside a panel about x 148-915, y 360-1162.

minors.description: The panel box sits inside its slot instead of filling it. Its top and bottom borders are about 14 px off panel 2.2's, and the gutter to the left of it is wider than standard, so the two-panel row does not line up the way Ch1's two-panel rows do.
minors.evidence: Panel 2.2 runs from y about 1517 to 2172. Panel 2.3's top border is visibly lower and its bottom border visibly higher, with cream gaps above and below it.

minors.description: The bottom row is off-centre. Panel 6.4 is flush to the left margin, panel 6.5 stops well short of the right margin, and the gutter between them is about 40 px against about 6 px everywhere else. Above them, rows 6.1/6.2 and 6.3 have different side margins again, so the page edges step in and out.
minors.evidence: 6.4 runs x 148-915 and 6.5 runs x 956-1653 (the right margin elsewhere is 1688). 6.3 runs x 185-1652, and 6.1/6.2 run x 219-1618.

minors.description: The order is reversed: the 'Tie it!' balloon sits higher than the caption, so it reads before 'He had said, in the dark below...'. The tail points at Nagoji's hands on the rope rather than his head, and the balloon covers the stretch of deck where the short throw lands.
minors.evidence: The 'Tie it! Around your chest! Quick!' balloon is at about x 862-1300, y 1123-1244. The caption is lower left at about x 150-702, y 1188-1314.

minors.description: The script places the caption inside the upper-left inset of Nagoji's hand on the rope coil. It is lettered at top right over Keshavrao's half of the panel instead.
minors.evidence: The 'For a moment I was nowhere. Only a body in a cold, roaring universe.' box is at about x 1040-1610, y 360-490. The inset is at x 148-615.

minors.description: The 'Keshavrao was gone.' caption box clips the fingertips of Nagoji's right hand.
minors.evidence: The caption is at about x 1341-1629, y 2217-2307, and the palm and thumb tip run into its left edge.

minors.description: The second caption sits right on the seam between the main image and the strip of insets, so it reads as part of the left inset (Keshavrao's hands).
minors.evidence: The 'Wait to free him, we both get smashed against the rail.' box is at about x 168-734, y 1872-2002, and its bottom edge lies on the inset boundary at about y 2000.

minors.description: The opening caption pair can read backwards. 'It was the change in the way the ship moved.' sits at the left edge of the panel, and 'The first warning was not the shout of a sailor...' sits at upper right, only slightly higher. A reader entering top-left may read the 'It was...' line first.
minors.evidence: In panel 1.1 the 'The first warning...' box spans y 285-375 at the right and the 'It was the change...' box spans y 370-435 at the far left. The script order is 'The first warning...' then 'It was the change...'.

minors.description: The establishing shot is level and warmly lit, and most prisoners in it are dozing. The script asks for a hold in near darkness with the whole image tilted hard, bodies sliding against one another and pen chains jerking sideways. The roll that is 'the first warning' is not shown.
minors.evidence: Panel 1.1 has a horizontal horizon and beams, a bright lantern-lit palette, and the men at right sit slumped with eyes closed. Nothing slides or swings.

minors.description: The sailors' shouts from above are lettered in calm, round, separate balloons. The script calls for jagged, overlapping balloons.
minors.evidence: In panel 1.3, 'Reef the sails! Haul, haul!' and 'Tie that down! Move, you son of a dog!' are smooth oval balloons that do not touch. Script: 'Jagged, overlapping balloons come from above and off panel.'

minors.description: Nagoji grips the beam with his hands far apart rather than hooking both forearms over the timber with his wrists together. Also, the script tags these two orders '(in Marathi)', and the adaptation notes say they are tagged as Marathi, but the balloons carry no language marker.
minors.evidence: In panel 3.2 his bandaged hands clutch the beam about two hand-widths apart. Both balloons ('Hold to the beams!...', 'Do not let the chain drag you.') are plain, with no bracket or translation note.

minors.description: The broadside wave reads as water running down a central aisle between level pens. The men are not thrown sideways or weightless, and most of them are bare-chested in loincloths rather than wearing the grey, brown and off-white rags set in 1.1.
minors.evidence: Panel 3.1 shows a straight corridor with a stream of white water, upright posts and men leaning on pen boards. The script asks that 'the hold is thrown sideways, men are almost weightless for a heartbeat'.

minors.description: The second balloon covers most of Nagoji's body and the area behind him, so the plank at the end of the pen bowing inward does not read. Keshavrao's foreground shoulder and arm are also heavily muscled, against his thin, narrow-shouldered lock.
minors.evidence: In panel 4.1 the 'You have seen the dungeon...' balloon fills roughly x 320-615, y 535-735, over Nagoji's torso and legs, and no bowed plank is visible. The over-shoulder Keshavrao in the left foreground has a bulky deltoid and biceps.

minors.description: Nagoji's head is cut off by the top panel border at about the brow line. His bared teeth still show, but the rounding-on move is cramped against the edge.
minors.evidence: In panel 5.3 (y 628-898) the top of Nagoji's hair and forehead are cropped at the panel's upper edge, and his eyes sit only a few pixels below the border.

minors.description: Keshavrao's 'Others.' and Nagoji's 'Quickly.' are close enough in height that the left balloon, 'Quickly.', can read first. The action is also static: both men sit on the beam rather than working along it, yanking rings and kicking at the wood.
minors.evidence: In panel 6.1 'Others.' spans y 330-400 at center-right and 'Quickly.' spans y 370-455 at left. The script order is KESHAVRAO: Others. then NAGOJI: Quickly. Both men are drawn seated on the beam.

minors.description: The caption 'For a moment I was nowhere. Only a body in a cold, roaring universe.' is lettered in the main image over Keshavrao, not inside the Nagoji inset as the script directs. Placed there, it reads as if it describes Keshavrao. The rain-washed graze at his hairline is not visible, and his arms are drawn heavily muscled against his thin lock.
minors.evidence: In panel 9.1 the caption box sits at upper right (x 748-1157, y 260-352) beside Keshavrao, while the upper-left inset of Nagoji's hand on the rope coil has no text. Script: 'The caption sits in the inset.'

minors.description: The rope-burn beat is soft. The palms are ordinary skin tone, not reddened or burned, and the rope lies across the open hands rather than visibly whipping through the grip toward the rail. The 10.1 caption ('The burns on my palms were the only proof') leans on this image.
minors.evidence: In panel 9.5 the hands are open with stripped bandage strips, the palm skin matches the forearm, and the rope runs evenly off the right edge. Script: 'the palms are reddened and burned... the severed tail whips through his grip and out of the panel toward the rail.'

minors.description: Nagoji looks down at his own hands rather than at the empty hatch, and the ladder is drawn intact, not broken. The script's 'looking at it' beat, the empty hatch as the object of his gaze, is lost.
minors.evidence: In panel 10.1 his head is bowed toward his open palms while the hatch sits off to the right, out of his eyeline. The ladder in the hatch has complete rungs and rails. Script: 'The empty hatch, the broken ladder... Nagoji... looking at it.'
